1: """Evaluation pipeline for the Spectral Composition paper (issue #49).
2: 
3: Owns all paper-table computations:
4: 
5: - Phase 1: train/val/test L1 reconstruction + lambda_ED ablation
6:   (``reconstruction_table``, ``ablation_table``).
7: - Phase 2: FAD-proxy (Frechet distance over frozen EnCodec feature
8:   distributions) + CLAP-proxy (cosine on a deterministic text/audio
9:   embedding) + baseline comparison (``frechet_distance``, ``fad_score``,
10:   ``text_embedding``, ``audio_embedding``, ``clap_proxy_score``).
11: - Phase 3a: dehydration compression ratio vs corpus size N
12:   (``compression_ratio``, ``compression_ratio_vs_n``).
13: - Phase 3b: rehydration coherence (MIDI pitch contour vs spectral
14:   centroid, Pearson r) (``rehydration_coherence``).
15: - Phase 3c: recursive variant diversity (pairwise CLAP-proxy cosine
16:   distance vs depth) (``variant_diversity``).
17: 
18: Dependency note. ``fadtk`` and ``laion-clap`` were removed from the project
19: due to dependency conflicts (see README "Open issues"). To stay green, the
20: Phase 2 / 3c "FAD" and "CLAP score" columns are implemented as faithful,
21: dependency-free proxies on the *same* frozen EnCodec feature space the model
22: already uses. The methodology is documented alongside each table so the
23: proxy columns are never mistaken for the original VGGish / LAION metrics.
24: 
25: This module must not define model architectures or training loops (per
26: AGENTS.md S11); it only evaluates already-trained components.
27: """
28: 
29: from __future__ import annotations
30: 
31: import hashlib
32: from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence
33: from pathlib import Path
34: 
35: import numpy as np
36: import torch
37: from torch import Tensor, nn
38: 
39: from ald_sc.arrow_prior import ArrowSpacePrior
40: from ald_sc.audio_codec import BaselineAudioDecoder, EnCodecEncoder
41: from ald_sc.losses import ALDSCLoss
42: 
43: __all__ = [
44:     "split_files",
45:     "evaluate_reconstruction",
46:     "reconstruction_table",
47:     "ablation_table",
48:     "frechet_distance",
49:     "encodec_pooled_features",
50:     "fad_score",
51:     "text_embedding",
52:     "audio_embedding",
53:     "clap_proxy_score",
54:     "perceptual_table",
55:     "compression_ratio",
56:     "compression_ratio_vs_n",
57:     "spectral_centroid",
58:     "midi_pitch_contour",
59:     "rehydration_coherence",
60:     "variant_diversity",
61: ]
62: 
63: SAMPLE_RATE = 24000
64: 
65: 
66: def split_files(
67:     files: Sequence[str | Path],
68:     train_frac: float = 0.7,
69:     val_frac: float = 0.15,
70:     seed: int = 3407,
71: ) -> tuple[list[Path], list[Path], list[Path]]:
72:     """Reproducible train/val/test split of a file list (mirrors nb06).
73: 
74:     The remainder after ``train_frac + val_frac`` goes to test. The split is
75:     seeded and the input list is sorted before shuffling so it is deterministic
76:     across runs and independent of the OS file order.
77:     """
78:     import random
79: 
80:     ordered = sorted(Path(f) for f in files)
81:     rng = random.Random(seed)
82:     shuffled = ordered[:]
83:     rng.shuffle(shuffled)
84:     n = len(shuffled)
85:     n_train = int(n * train_frac)
86:     n_val = int(n * val_frac)
87:     train = shuffled[:n_train]
88:     val = shuffled[n_train : n_train + n_val]
89:     test = shuffled[n_train + n_val :]
90:     return train, val, test
91: 
92: 
93: @torch.no_grad()
94: def evaluate_reconstruction(
95:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
96:     decoder: nn.Module,
97:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
98:     loader,
99:     loss_fn: ALDSCLoss,
100:     device: torch.device,
101:     use_cspec: bool = True,
102: ) -> dict[str, float]:
103:     """Mean reconstruction metrics of a decoder over a loader.
104: 
105:     Handles both graph decoders (which take ``(z, c_spec)``) and the matched
106:     baseline (which takes ``z`` only). When ``use_cspec`` is False the graph
107:     decoder receives a zeroed ``c_spec`` — the lambda_ED ablation.
108:     """
109:     encoder = encoder.to(device).eval()
110:     decoder = decoder.to(device).eval()
111:     prior = prior.to(device)
112:     is_baseline = isinstance(decoder, BaselineAudioDecoder)
113: 
114:     totals = {"rec": 0.0, "stft": 0.0, "chart": 0.0, "smooth": 0.0}
115:     n = 0
116:     for batch in loader:
117:         x = batch.to(device) if isinstance(batch, Tensor) else batch[0].to(device)
118:         z, A, c_spec = encoder.encode(x, prior)
119:         if is_baseline:
120:             x_hat = decoder(z)
121:         elif use_cspec:
122:             x_hat = decoder(z, c_spec)
123:         else:
124:             x_hat = decoder(z, torch.zeros_like(c_spec))
125:         losses = loss_fn(x, x_hat, A, A.detach())
126:         totals["rec"] += float(losses["rec"].item())
127:         totals["stft"] += float(losses["stft"].item())
128:         totals["chart"] += float(losses["chart"].item())
129:         totals["smooth"] += float(losses["smooth"].item())
130:         n += 1
131:     return {k: v / max(n, 1) for k, v in totals.items()}
132: 
133: 
134: def reconstruction_table(
135:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
136:     graph_decoder: nn.Module,
137:     baseline_decoder: nn.Module,
138:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
139:     loss_fn: ALDSCLoss,
140:     loaders: dict[str, object],
141:     device: torch.device,
142: ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
143:     """Phase 1, Table 1: mean L1 reconstruction per split per decoder.
144: 
145:     Returns one row per (split, decoder) with columns
146:     ``split, decoder, L1, stft, chart, smooth``.
147:     """
148:     rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
149:     for split_name, loader in loaders.items():
150:         for dec_name, dec in (("graph", graph_decoder), ("baseline", baseline_decoder)):
151:             m = evaluate_reconstruction(encoder, dec, prior, loader, loss_fn, device)
152:             rows.append(
153:                 {
154:                     "split": split_name,
155:                     "decoder": dec_name,
156:                     "L1": m["rec"],
157:                     "stft": m["stft"],
158:                     "chart": m["chart"],
159:                     "smooth": m["smooth"],
160:                 }
161:             )
162:     return rows
163: 
164: 
165: def ablation_table(
166:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
167:     graph_decoder: nn.Module,
168:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
169:     loss_fn: ALDSCLoss,
170:     loaders: dict[str, object],
171:     device: torch.device,
172: ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
173:     """Phase 1, Table 2: lambda_ED ablation (c_spec on vs off).
174: 
175:     For each split reports the graph-decoder L1 with and without c_spec
176:     gating, plus the lambda_ED delta (without - with; negative means gating
177:     helps reconstruction). Columns: ``split, with_cspec, L1`` and a final
178:     delta row per split.
179:     """
180:     rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
181:     for split_name, loader in loaders.items():
182:         with_c = evaluate_reconstruction(
183:             encoder, graph_decoder, prior, loader, loss_fn, device, use_cspec=True
184:         )
185:         without = evaluate_reconstruction(
186:             encoder, graph_decoder, prior, loader, loss_fn, device, use_cspec=False
187:         )
188:         rows.append({"split": split_name, "with_cspec": True, "L1": with_c["rec"]})
189:         rows.append({"split": split_name, "with_cspec": False, "L1": without["rec"]})
190:         rows.append(
191:             {
192:                 "split": split_name,
193:                 "with_cspec": "delta",
194:                 "L1": without["rec"] - with_c["rec"],
195:             }
196:         )
197:     return rows
198: 
199: 
200: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
201: # Phase 2: perceptual metrics (dependency-free proxies)
202: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
203: 
204: 
205: @torch.no_grad()
206: def encodec_pooled_features(
207:     audio_iter: Iterable[Tensor],
208:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
209:     device: torch.device,
210: ) -> Tensor:
211:     """Concatenate pooled EnCodec features (N, F) for an iterable of clips.
212: 
213:     ``audio_iter`` yields waveforms shaped (B, 1, T_audio) or (B, T_audio) or
214:     (1, 1, T_audio). Batched inputs produce multiple feature vectors.
215:     Returns a single (N, F) tensor where N is the total number of clips.
216:     """
217:     encoder = encoder.to(device).eval()
218:     feats: list[Tensor] = []
219:     for clip in audio_iter:
220:         x = clip.to(device)
221:         if x.dim() == 2:
222:             x = x.unsqueeze(0)
223:         if x.dim() == 3 and x.shape[1] != 1:
224:             x = x.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True)
225:         z = encoder.extract_features(x)
226:         feats.append(z.mean(dim=2).cpu())
227:     return torch.cat(feats, dim=0)
228: 
229: 
230: def frechet_distance(feats_a: Tensor, feats_b: Tensor) -> float:
231:     """Frechet distance between two feature distributions.
232: 
233:     ``||mu_a - mu_b||^2 + Tr(C_a + C_b - 2 (C_a C_b)^{1/2})`` on per-sample
234:     feature vectors. This is the Frechet Audio Distance formula evaluated on
235:     EnCodec pooled features (the FAD-proxy used here).
236:     """
237:     a = feats_a.detach().float()
238:     b = feats_b.detach().float()
239:     if a.dim() != 2 or b.dim() != 2:
240:         raise ValueError("frechet_distance expects (N, F) feature matrices")
241:     mu_a = a.mean(dim=0)
242:     mu_b = b.mean(dim=0)
243:     ca = torch.cov(a.T)
244:     cb = torch.cov(b.T)
245:     diff = (mu_a - mu_b).pow(2).sum().item()
246:     # eigenvalues of (Ca @ Cb) are real nonneg for PSD factors; sqrt-sum is
247:     # Tr(sqrt(Ca Cb)). Guard with symmetric sqrt via Ca^(1/2) Cb Ca^(1/2).
248:     eigvals_a, eigvecs_a = torch.linalg.eigh(ca)
249:     eigvals_a = eigvals_a.clamp(min=0)
250:     sqrt_ca = (eigvecs_a * eigvals_a.sqrt().unsqueeze(0)) @ eigvecs_a.T
251:     mid = sqrt_ca @ cb @ sqrt_ca
252:     mid = (mid + mid.T) / 2
253:     eigvals_mid = torch.linalg.eigvalsh(mid).clamp(min=0)
254:     trace_term = float(eigvals_mid.sqrt().sum().item())
255:     ca_reg = float(torch.trace(ca).item())
256:     cb_reg = float(torch.trace(cb).item())
257:     return float(diff + ca_reg + cb_reg - 2.0 * trace_term)
258: 
259: 
260: def fad_score(generated_features: Tensor, reference_features: Tensor) -> float:
261:     """FAD-proxy: Frechet distance between generated and reference feature sets.
262: 
263:     Lower is better (generated distribution closer to the reference corpus).
264:     Falls back to a simple ||mu|| difference when either set has < 2 samples
265:     (a covariance needs at least 2 points).
266:     """
267:     if generated_features.shape[0] < 2 or reference_features.shape[0] < 2:
268:         return float(
269:             (generated_features.mean(0) - reference_features.mean(0))
270:             .pow(2)
271:             .sum()
272:             .item()
273:         )
274:     val = frechet_distance(generated_features, reference_features)
275:     return max(val, 0.0)
276: 
277: 
278: def text_embedding(text: str, dim: int, salt: int = 0) -> Tensor:
279:     """Deterministic text -> dim embedding (CLAP-proxy text side).
280: 
281:     A hashing bag-of-characters projection that is fully determined by the
282:     string (and an optional salt). The result is L2-normalised. This is *not*
283:     a learned text encoder; it gives a stable, reproducible target vector so
284:     the cosine-alignment score is well defined and responds to the prompt.
285:     """
286:     vec = torch.zeros(dim, dtype=torch.float32)
287:     digest = hashlib.sha256(f"{salt}:{text}".encode("utf-8")).digest()
288:     # Walk the hash bytes, scattering signed contributions across dim. Iterate
289:     # the digest cyclically so the vector is dense for short strings.
290:     i = 0
291:     while vec.abs().sum().item() == 0 or i < max(8, dim):
292:         chunk = hashlib.sha256(digest + i.to_bytes(4, "little")).digest()
293:         for byte in chunk:
294:             sign = 1.0 if (byte & 1) else -1.0
295:             mag = ((byte >> 1) & 0x7F) / 127.0
296:             vec[(i + (byte >> 1)) % dim] += sign * mag
297:             i += 1
298:             if vec.abs().sum().item() > 0 and i >= max(8, dim):
299:                 break
300:         if i >= max(256, dim * 4):
301:             break
302:     norm = vec.norm()
303:     if norm > 0:
304:         vec = vec / norm
305:     return vec
306: 
307: 
308: @torch.no_grad()
309: def audio_embedding(
310:     audio: Tensor | Iterable[Tensor],
311:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
312:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior | None,
313:     device: torch.device,
314: ) -> Tensor:
315:     """CLAP-proxy audio side: pooled EnCodec features of one or many clips.
316: 
317:     Accepts a single (1, 1, T) clip or an iterable of clips and returns a
318:     single (F,) mean feature (for a single clip) or (N, F) features. Normalised
319:     to unit norm so cosine similarity is well scaled.
320:     """
321:     if isinstance(audio, Tensor):
322:         audio = [audio]
323:     feats = encodec_pooled_features(audio, encoder, device)
324:     if feats.shape[0] == 1:
325:         v = feats[0]
326:     else:
327:         v = feats.mean(dim=0)
328:     norm = v.norm()
329:     if norm > 0:
330:         v = v / norm
331:     return v
332: 
333: 
334: def clap_proxy_score(
335:     generated_audio: list[Tensor],
336:     text_prompt: str,
337:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
338:     device: torch.device,
339: ) -> float:
340:     """Mean cosine similarity between generated clips and a text prompt.
341: 
342:     Audio side = L2-normalised mean EnCodec-pooled feature of the generated
343:     bank; text side = L2-normalised deterministic hashing embedding of the
344:     prompt into the same F dimensions. Returns a scalar in [-1, 1]. This is the
345:     documented CLAP-proxy (not LAION-CLAP).
346:     """
347:     audio_vec = audio_embedding(generated_audio, encoder, None, device)
348:     feat_dim = audio_vec.shape[0]
349:     text_vec = text_embedding(text_prompt, feat_dim).to(audio_vec.device)
350:     return float(torch.cosine_similarity(audio_vec, text_vec, dim=0).item())
351: 
352: 
353: def perceptual_table(
354:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
355:     graph_decoder: nn.Module,
356:     baseline_decoder: nn.Module,
357:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
358:     dit: nn.Module,
359:     sched,
360:     reference_features: Tensor,
361:     text_prompt: str,
362:     device: torch.device,
363:     n_gen: int = 16,
364:     steps: int = 50,
365:     seed: int = 3407,
366: ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
367:     """Phase 2, Table 3: FAD-proxy + CLAP-proxy for graph vs baseline.
368: 
369:     Generates ``n_gen`` latents via DDIM, decodes with each decoder, and
370:     compares the resulting audio feature distribution to ``reference_features``
371:     (the held-out test-set EnCodec features). Also reports the CLAP-proxy
372:     alignment between the generated bank and ``text_prompt``.
373:     """
374:     from ald_sc.sampling import sample_ddim
375: 
376:     rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
377:     encoder = encoder.to(device).eval()
378:     prior = prior.to(device)
379:     dit = dit.to(device).eval()
380: 
381:     def _gen_audio(decoder, use_cspec: bool) -> list[Tensor]:
382:         clips: list[Tensor] = []
383:         for i in range(n_gen):
384:             z = sample_ddim(
385:                 dit,
386:                 sched,
387:                 batch_size=1,
388:                 steps=steps,
389:                 seed=seed + i,
390:                 device=device,
391:             )
392:             a = z.mean(dim=2)
393:             c_spec = prior.chart_energy_descriptor(a)
394:             if isinstance(decoder, BaselineAudioDecoder):
395:                 x_hat = decoder(z)
396:             elif use_cspec:
397:                 x_hat = decoder(z, c_spec)
398:             else:
399:                 x_hat = decoder(z, torch.zeros_like(c_spec))
400:             x_hat = x_hat.clamp(-1, 1).squeeze(0)
401:             peak = x_hat.abs().max()
402:             if peak > 0:
403:                 x_hat = x_hat / peak
404:             clips.append(x_hat.unsqueeze(0))
405:         return clips
406: 
407:     for name, dec, use_c in (
408:         ("graph", graph_decoder, True),
409:         ("baseline", baseline_decoder, False),
410:     ):
411:         clips = _gen_audio(dec, use_c)
412:         gen_feats = encodec_pooled_features(clips, encoder, device)
413:         # Both feature sets are on CPU (encodec_pooled_features moves to CPU).
414:         fad = fad_score(gen_feats, reference_features.cpu())
415:         clap = clap_proxy_score(clips, text_prompt, encoder, device)
416:         rows.append(
417:             {
418:                 "decoder": name,
419:                 "FAD": fad,
420:                 "FAD_method": "encod_proxy",
421:                 "CLAP": clap,
422:                 "CLAP_method": "encod_proxy",
423:             }
424:         )
425:     return rows
426: 
427: 
428: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
429: # Phase 3a: dehydration compression ratio
430: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
431: 
432: 
433: def _prior_float_count(prior: ArrowSpacePrior) -> int:
434:     """Number of float32 values stored in the dehydrated prior."""
435:     n = 0
436:     for buf_name in ("L_F", "U_q", "eigvals_q", "lambdas_ed", "lambdas_chart"):
437:         buf = getattr(prior, buf_name, None)
438:         if buf is not None:
439:             n += int(buf.numel())
440:     return n
441: 
442: 
443: def compression_ratio(
444:     n_clips: int,
445:     audio_length: int,
446:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
447:     bits_per_pcm_sample: int = 16,
448:     bits_per_latent_element: int = 16,
449:     latent_length: int | None = None,
450:     latent_channels: int = 128,
451:     encod_bandwidth_kbps: int = 24,
452:     use_code_rate: bool = True,
453: ) -> dict[str, float]:
454:     """Dehydration compression ratio for a corpus of ``n_clips``.
455: 
456:     Two representations are compared:
457: 
458:     - **Raw audio**: ``n_clips * audio_length * bits_per_pcm_sample`` bits
459:       (16-bit PCM library).
460:     - **Dehydrated**: the shared ArrowSpace prior
461:       ``(L_F, U_q, eigvals_q, lambda_ED, lambda_chart)`` stored once (in
462:       float32 = 32 bits/value) plus per-clip latent storage. The latent
463:       storage models EnCodec's actual compressed rate:
464:       ``encod_bandwidth_kbps * (audio_length / sample_rate)`` bits/clip. Set
465:       ``use_code_rate=False`` to instead count latent tensors as
466:       ``latent_channels * latent_length * bits_per_latent_element``.
467: 
468:     Returns raw/dehydrated bit counts and the ratio raw/dehydrated. The
469:     prior is constant across N, so the ratio grows with N and asymptotes to
470:     the per-clip code rate ratio (the prior amortises).
471:     """
472:     raw_bits = float(n_clips * audio_length * bits_per_pcm_sample)
473:     prior_bits = float(_prior_float_count(prior) * 32)
474:     if use_code_rate:
475:         latent_bits_per_clip = float(
476:             encod_bandwidth_kbps * 1000 * (audio_length / SAMPLE_RATE)
477:         )
478:     else:
479:         if latent_length is None:
480:             latent_length = audio_length // 320
481:         latent_bits_per_clip = float(
482:             latent_channels * latent_length * bits_per_latent_element
483:         )
484:     dehydrated_bits = prior_bits + n_clips * latent_bits_per_clip
485:     ratio = raw_bits / dehydrated_bits if dehydrated_bits > 0 else float("inf")
486:     return {
487:         "N": n_clips,
488:         "raw_bits": raw_bits,
489:         "prior_bits": prior_bits,
490:         "latent_bits_per_clip": latent_bits_per_clip,
491:         "dehydrated_bits": dehydrated_bits,
492:         "compression_ratio": ratio,
493:     }
494: 
495: 
496: def compression_ratio_vs_n(
497:     n_values: Sequence[int],
498:     audio_length: int,
499:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
500:     **kwargs,
501: ) -> list[dict[str, float]]:
502:     """Compression ratio as a function of corpus size N (Table 4 rows)."""
503:     return [compression_ratio(n, audio_length, prior, **kwargs) for n in n_values]
504: 
505: 
506: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
507: # Phase 3b: rehydration coherence
508: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
509: 
510: 
511: def spectral_centroid(
512:     audio: Tensor, sample_rate: int = SAMPLE_RATE, n_fft: int = 2048, hop: int = 512
513: ) -> Tensor:
514:     """Per-frame spectral centroid (1-D tensor) of a mono waveform.
515: 
516:     centroid(t) = sum_f f * |X(t,f)| / sum_f |X(t,f)|.
517: 
518:     Accepts (T,) or (1, T) or (1, 1, T). Returns (num_frames,) centroid in Hz.
519:     """
520:     x = audio.detach().float().cpu()
521:     if x.dim() == 3:
522:         x = x.squeeze(0).squeeze(0)
523:     elif x.dim() == 2:
524:         x = x.squeeze(0)
525:     window = torch.hann_window(n_fft)
526:     spec = torch.stft(
527:         x,
528:         n_fft,
529:         hop_length=hop,
530:         return_complex=True,
531:         window=window,
532:     )
533:     mag = spec.abs().clamp(min=1e-12)
534:     freqs = torch.linspace(0, sample_rate / 2, mag.shape[0])
535:     centroid = (freqs[:, None] * mag).sum(dim=0) / mag.sum(dim=0)
536:     return centroid
537: 
538: 
539: def midi_pitch_contour(
540:     events: Sequence[tuple[int, float, float]],
541:     num_frames: int,
542:     sample_rate: int = SAMPLE_RATE,
543:     hop: int = 512,
544: ) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
545:     """Sample the MIDI pitch contour (semitones) at the centroid frame times.
546: 
547:     Returns ``(contour, mask)`` of length ``num_frames``. ``mask`` is True on
548:     frames where a note is active; ``contour`` is the MIDI note number on
549:     active frames and 0 elsewhere.
550:     """
551:     times = torch.arange(num_frames) * hop / sample_rate
552:     contour = torch.zeros(num_frames)
553:     mask = torch.zeros(num_frames, dtype=torch.bool)
554:     for note, start, dur in sorted(events, key=lambda e: e[1]):
555:         lo = start
556:         hi = start + dur
557:         active = (times >= lo) & (times < hi)
558:         contour[active] = float(note)
559:         mask[active] = True
560:     return contour, mask
561: 
562: 
563: def rehydration_coherence(
564:     model,
565:     events: Sequence[tuple[int, float, float]],
566:     bank,
567:     pitch_bank_root: int = 60,
568: ) -> dict[str, object]:
569:     """Phase 3b: coherence of a rehydrated render vs its MIDI score.
570: 
571:     Renders ``events`` with ``model.synthesize_midi`` (Mode C), computes the
572:     spectral-centroid contour of the render, the MIDI pitch contour sampled at
573:     the same frames, and reports the Pearson correlation between the two over
574:     frames where a note is active. A higher r means the rehydrated audio's
575:     spectral centroid tracks the scored pitch contour.
576:     """
577:     audio = model.synthesize_midi(
578:         list(events), list(bank), pitch_bank_root=pitch_bank_root, seed=3407
579:     )
580:     sr = model.sample_rate
581:     centroid = spectral_centroid(audio, sample_rate=sr)
582:     num_frames = centroid.shape[0]
583:     contour, mask = midi_pitch_contour(events, num_frames, sample_rate=sr)
584:     if mask.sum() >= 2:
585:         a = contour[mask].numpy().astype(np.float64)
586:         b = centroid[mask].numpy().astype(np.float64)
587:         if a.std() > 0 and b.std() > 0:
588:             r = float(np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1])
589:         else:
590:             r = 0.0
591:     else:
592:         r = float("nan")
593:     n_notes = int(mask.sum().item())
594:     return {
595:         "midi_events": len(events),
596:         "active_frames": n_notes,
597:         "pearson_r": r,
598:         "centroid_mean_hz": float(centroid.mean().item()),
599:         "centroid_std_hz": float(centroid.std().item()),
600:     }
601: 
602: 
603: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
604: # Phase 3c: recursive variant diversity
605: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
606: 
607: 
608: def variant_diversity(
609:     make_variants,
610:     depths: Sequence[int],
611:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
612:     device: torch.device,
613: ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
614:     """Mean pairwise CLAP-proxy cosine *distance* vs recursion depth.
615: 
616:     ``make_variants(d)`` must return a list of ``d`` audio clips (one per
617:     distinct MIDI at "depth" d). The function embeds them via the FAD-proxy
618:     audio embedding and reports the mean pairwise cosine distance
619:     (1 - cosine) among them; depth 1 trivially yields 0.0 (a single variant
620:     has no inter-variant distance).
621: 
622:     Returns one row per depth: ``depth, n_variants, mean_distance,
623:     min_distance, max_distance``.
624:     """
625:     rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
626:     for d in depths:
627:         clips = list(make_variants(d))
628:         if d <= 1 or len(clips) < 2:
629:             rows.append(
630:                 {
631:                     "depth": d,
632:                     "n_variants": len(clips),
633:                     "mean_distance": 0.0,
634:                     "min_distance": 0.0,
635:                     "max_distance": 0.0,
636:                 }
637:             )
638:             continue
639:         feats = encodec_pooled_features(clips, encoder, device)
640:         feats = feats.to(device)
641:         norms = feats.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp(min=1e-12)
642:         unit = feats / norms
643:         sim = unit @ unit.T
644:         dist = 1.0 - sim
645:         iu = torch.triu_indices(d, d, offset=1)
646:         pairs = dist[iu[0], iu[1]]
647:         rows.append(
648:             {
649:                 "depth": d,
650:                 "n_variants": d,
651:                 "mean_distance": float(pairs.mean().item()),
652:                 "min_distance": float(pairs.min().item()),
653:                 "max_distance": float(pairs.max().item()),
654:             }
655:         )
656:     return rows
657: 
658: 
659: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
660: # CSV writer helper
661: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
662: 
663: 
664: def write_csv(path: str | Path, rows: Sequence[dict[str, object]]) -> None:
665:     """Write a list of homogeneous dicts to a CSV (header from first row keys)."""
666:     import csv
667: 
668:     path = Path(path)
669:     path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
670:     if not rows:
671:         path.write_text("")
672:         return
673:     fieldnames = list(rows[0].keys())
674:     with open(path, "w", newline="") as f:
675:         writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)
676:         writer.writeheader()
677:         for row in rows:
678:             writer.writerow(row)

# Autoresearch plan — Issue #50 Phase 1: evaluation extensions + MPS rerun

`[autoresearch] mode: orchestrator (build-feature)`

## Goal
Extend the evaluation pipeline per issue #50 Phase 1, rerun all deliverables on
MPS with the new grad-clip trainer (issue #51 fixes), and calibrate the
experiment framing to the paper's objective: **presenting a novel paradigm** —
a workflow introduction with scientific backing, not a benchmark claim.

## Calibration intent (user-confirmed direction)
- The paper introduces a novel workflow (dehydration → diffusion → rehydration
  → recursive variation) backed by honest preliminary-scale measurements.
- No "beats the baseline" claims: numbers are hypothesis-generating evidence
  at N=256/20-epoch scale, with explicit hypotheses for what should improve
  at scale (training length, N, capacity).
- Workflow-affordance metrics (compression, coherence, variant drift,
  diversity-vs-fidelity tradeoffs) stand alongside fidelity metrics; FAD/CLAP
  stay documented proxies.
- Every table carries methodology columns; summary reports numbers verbatim.

## Scope
- `src/ald_sc/eval.py` additions (+ unit tests in `tests/test_eval.py`):
  - `band_energy_retention` — per-mode band energies of original vs
    reconstructed audio via `prior.band_energies` (§6.2 per-band retention).
  - `spectral_rolloff` — companion to `spectral_centroid` (§6.1 rolloff drift).
  - `recursive_variant_drift` — TRUE R-round recursion: feed outputs back
    through `condition_on_audio` → `synthesize_midi`; centroid/rolloff drift
    + CLAP-proxy distance to round 0 (replaces the MIDI-rotation hack).
  - `eps_sweep` — heat-death ε sweep helper (sampling-only, SpectralSchedule).
- `scripts/run_evaluation.py`:
  - `--ablation-q {4,8,16,32}` (decoder retraining per prior),
    `--ablation-noise {0.0,0.1,0.25,0.5}` (diversity-vs-fidelity),
    `--ablation-eps {1e-2,1e-3,1e-4}` (sampling-only).
  - Checkpoints to `results/artifacts/` (gitignored) so sweeps share the
    encoder/prior embeddings.
  - Integrate retention + rolloff + true recursion into the main run.

- Runs (all `--device mps`):
  - Main NSynth 256-subset run with new metrics integrated.

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Phase 1 extension: per-band spectral energy retention (paper §6.2)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


@torch.no_grad()
def band_energy_retention(
    encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
    decoder: nn.Module,
    prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
    loader,
    device: torch.device,
    use_cspec: bool = True,
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Per-mode band-energy retention of reconstructions (paper §6.2).

    For each batch: encode the original audio to ``A`` (pooled EnCodec
    features), decode to ``x_hat``, re-encode ``x_hat`` to ``A_hat``, and
    compare the normalised per-mode band energies ``e_tilde`` via
    ``prior.band_energies``. Retention per mode k is
    ``e_tilde_rec[k] / e_tilde_orig[k]`` (1.0 = perfect retention; guarded
    to 0 when the original mode carries negligible energy).

    Returns one row per spectral mode k with columns
    ``k, e_orig, e_recon, retention, cosine`` where cosine is the mean
    cosine similarity between the original and reconstructed band-energy
    vectors (repeated across rows as the split-level summary).
    """
    encoder = encoder.to(device).eval()
    decoder = decoder.to(device).eval()
    prior = prior.to(device)
    is_baseline = isinstance(decoder, BaselineAudioDecoder)

    e_orig_sum = torch.zeros(prior.q)
    e_rec_sum = torch.zeros(prior.q)
    cos_sum, n_batches = 0.0, 0
    for batch in loader:
        x = batch.to(device) if isinstance(batch, Tensor) else batch[0].to(device)
        z, A, c_spec = encoder.encode(x, prior)
        if is_baseline:
            x_hat = decoder(z)
        elif use_cspec:
            x_hat = decoder(z, c_spec)
        else:
            x_hat = decoder(z, torch.zeros_like(c_spec))
        _, A_hat, _ = encoder.encode(x_hat.clamp(-1, 1), prior)

        e_o = prior.band_energies(A)
        e_r = prior.band_energies(A_hat)
        e_o = e_o / (e_o.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-8)
        e_r = e_r / (e_r.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-8)
        e_orig_sum += e_o.sum(dim=0).cpu()
        e_rec_sum += e_r.sum(dim=0).cpu()
        cos = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(e_o, e_r, dim=-1)
        cos_sum += float(cos.mean().item())
        n_batches += 1

    if n_batches == 0:
        return []
    e_orig_mean = e_orig_sum / n_batches
    e_rec_mean = e_rec_sum / n_batches
    cosine = cos_sum / n_batches
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for k in range(prior.q):
        retention = (
            float(e_rec_mean[k] / e_orig_mean[k])
            if e_orig_mean[k] > 1e-6
            else 0.0
        )
        rows.append(
            {
                "k": k,
                "e_orig": float(e_orig_mean[k]),
                "e_recon": float(e_rec_mean[k]),
                "retention": retention,
                "cosine": cosine,
            }
        )
    return rows

def spectral_rolloff(
    audio: Tensor,
    sample_rate: int = SAMPLE_RATE,
    n_fft: int = 2048,
    hop: int = 512,
    fraction: float = 0.85,
) -> Tensor:
    """Per-frame spectral rolloff (1-D tensor) of a mono waveform.

    rolloff(t) = the lowest frequency f such that ``fraction`` of the
    frame's spectral energy is contained in bins <= f (classic 0.85
    rolloff). Accepts (T,), (1, T) or (1, 1, T). Returns (num_frames,)
    rolloff frequencies in Hz.
    """
    x = audio.detach().float().cpu()
    if x.dim() == 3:
        x = x.squeeze(0).squeeze(0)
    elif x.dim() == 2:
        x = x.squeeze(0)
    window = torch.hann_window(n_fft)
    spec = torch.stft(
        x,
        n_fft,
        hop_length=hop,
        return_complex=True,
        window=window,
    )
    mag = spec.abs().clamp(min=0.0)
    freqs = torch.linspace(0, sample_rate / 2, mag.shape[0])
    energy = mag.pow(2)
    cum = torch.cumsum(energy, dim=0)
    total = cum[-1:, :]
    crossed = cum >= fraction * total
    # First bin where the cumulative energy crosses the fraction threshold.
    idx = crossed.float().argmax(dim=0)
    return freqs[idx]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Phase 3c extension: TRUE recursive variant drift (paper §6.1, Stage 4)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def recursive_variant_drift(
    model,
    events: Sequence[tuple[int, float, float]],
    rounds: int,
    encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
    device: torch.device,
    steps: int = 50,
    seed: int = 3407,
    bank_n: int = 4,
    strength: float = 0.5,
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """True R-round recursion: feed outputs back through the workflow.

    Round 0 renders ``events`` from a freshly generated bank. Round r
    conditions on the previous round's render (``condition_on_audio``),
    rebuilds the bank, and re-renders the same score (``synthesize_midi``).
    Reports per round: spectral centroid / rolloff means (drift) and the
    CLAP-proxy cosine distance of the round's render to the round-0 render
    (cumulative novelty). This replaces the earlier MIDI-rotation
    approximation of "depth" with faithful recursive feeding.
    """
    bank = model.generate_sound_bank(n=bank_n, steps=steps, seed=seed)
    audio = model.synthesize_midi(list(events), list(bank), seed=seed)
    audio = audio.detach().cpu().unsqueeze(0) if audio.dim() == 2 else audio.cpu()

    base_feat = encodec_pooled_features([audio], encoder, device)[0]
    base_feat = base_feat / base_feat.norm().clamp(min=1e-12)

    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []

    def _row(r: int, clip: Tensor) -> dict[str, object]:
        centroid = spectral_centroid(clip, sample_rate=model.sample_rate)
        rolloff = spectral_rolloff(clip, sample_rate=model.sample_rate)
        feat = encodec_pooled_features([clip], encoder, device)[0]
        feat = feat / feat.norm().clamp(min=1e-12)
        dist = 1.0 - float(torch.dot(feat, base_feat).item())
        return {
            "round": r,
            "centroid_mean_hz": float(centroid.mean().item()),
            "centroid_std_hz": float(centroid.std().item()),
            "rolloff_mean_hz": float(rolloff.mean().item()),
            "clap_distance_to_round0": max(dist, 0.0),
        }

    rows.append(_row(0, audio))
    for r in range(1, rounds + 1):
        variants = model.condition_on_audio(
            audio, n=bank_n, steps=steps, strength=strength, seed=seed + r
        )
        audio = model.synthesize_midi(
            list(events), list(variants), seed=seed + r
        ).detach()
        audio = audio.unsqueeze(0) if audio.dim() == 2 else audio
        rows.append(_row(r, audio))
    return rows


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Phase 4: heat-death epsilon sweep (sampling-only)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


@torch.no_grad()
def eps_sweep(
    dit: nn.Module,
    sched,
    prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
    decoder: nn.Module,
    encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
    reference_features: Tensor,
    eps_values: Sequence[float],
    device: torch.device,
    n_gen: int = 8,
    steps: int = 50,
    seed: int = 3407,
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Heat-death stopping sweep: steps used + FAD-proxy vs epsilon.

    For each epsilon a :class:`SpectralSchedule` with that heat-death
    threshold drives DDIM early stopping. Reports mean steps actually used,
    the FAD-proxy of the generated bank against ``reference_features``,
    and the per-generation step counts. Sampling-only: no retraining.
    Larger epsilon stops earlier (fewer steps, faster, potentially worse).
    """
    from ald_sc.sampling import sample_ddim
    from ald_sc.spectral_schedule import SpectralSchedule

    dit = dit.to(device).eval()
    decoder = decoder.to(device).eval()
    prior = prior.to(device)
    encoder = encoder.to(device).eval()

    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for eps in eps_values:
        spec_sched = SpectralSchedule(prior=prior, horizon=1.0, eps=float(eps))
        clips: list[Tensor] = []
        steps_used: list[int] = []
        for i in range(n_gen):
            z, used = sample_ddim(
                dit,
                sched,
                batch_size=1,
                steps=steps,
                seed=seed + i,
                device=device,
                spectral_schedule=spec_sched,
                return_steps=True,
            )
            a = z.mean(dim=2)
            c_spec = prior.chart_energy_descriptor(a)
            if isinstance(decoder, BaselineAudioDecoder):
                x_hat = decoder(z)
            else:
                x_hat = decoder(z, c_spec)
            x_hat = x_hat.clamp(-1, 1).squeeze(0)
            peak = x_hat.abs().max()
            if peak > 0:
                x_hat = x_hat / peak
            clips.append(x_hat.unsqueeze(0))
            steps_used.append(int(used))
        gen_feats = encodec_pooled_features(clips, encoder, device)
        fad = fad_score(gen_feats, reference_features.cpu())
        rows.append(
            {
                "eps": float(eps),
                "mean_steps": sum(steps_used) / len(steps_used),
                "min_steps": min(steps_used),
                "max_steps": max(steps_used),
                "FAD": fad,
                "FAD_method": "encod_proxy",
                "n_gen": n_gen,
            }
        )
    return rows

class TestBandEnergyRetention:
    def _loader(self):
        ds = ToyAudioDataset(num_samples=8, audio_length=24000)
        return build_audio_dataloader(ds, batch_size=4, shuffle=False)

    def test_one_row_per_mode(self) -> None:
        prior = _toy_prior(q=4)
        encoder = _StubEncoder()
        dec = _TinyGraphDecoder()
        rows = band_energy_retention(
            encoder, dec, prior, self._loader(), torch.device("cpu")
        )
        assert len(rows) == prior.q
        for r in rows:
            assert {"k", "e_orig", "e_recon", "retention", "cosine"} <= set(r)
            assert r["e_orig"] >= 0.0 and r["e_recon"] >= 0.0
            assert -1.0 <= r["cosine"] <= 1.0

    def test_normalized_band_energies(self) -> None:
        prior = _toy_prior(q=4)
        encoder = _StubEncoder()
        dec = _TinyGraphDecoder()
        rows = band_energy_retention(
            encoder, dec, prior, self._loader(), torch.device("cpu")
        )
        total = sum(r["e_orig"] for r in rows)
        assert abs(total - 1.0) < 0.05  # e_tilde sums to ~1

    def test_cspec_off_sends_zeros(self) -> None:
        prior = _toy_prior(q=4)
        encoder = _StubEncoder()
        captured: dict[str, object] = {}

        class _SpyDecoder(_TinyGraphDecoder):
            def forward(self, z, c_spec=None):  # type: ignore[override]
                captured["c_spec"] = c_spec
                return super().forward(z, c_spec)

        band_energy_retention(
            encoder,
            _SpyDecoder(),
            prior,
            self._loader(),
            torch.device("cpu"),
            use_cspec=False,
        )
        assert captured["c_spec"] is not None
        assert float(captured["c_spec"].abs().sum()) == 0.0  # type: ignore[union-attr]

class TestSpectralRolloff:
    def test_sine_rolloff_below_high_freq(self) -> None:
        sr = 24000
        t = torch.arange(sr, dtype=torch.float32) / sr
        x = torch.sin(2 * torch.pi * 500.0 * t)
        ro = spectral_rolloff(x, sample_rate=sr)
        assert ro.dim() == 1
        assert 0.0 < ro.mean().item() < 5000.0

    def test_noise_rolloff_above_sine(self) -> None:
        sr = 24000
        t = torch.arange(sr, dtype=torch.float32) / sr
        sine = torch.sin(2 * torch.pi * 500.0 * t)
        noise = torch.randn(sr) * 0.1
        ro_sine = spectral_rolloff(sine, sample_rate=sr).mean().item()
        ro_noise = spectral_rolloff(noise, sample_rate=sr).mean().item()
        assert ro_noise > ro_sine

    def test_shape_variants(self) -> None:
        x = torch.randn(24000)
        for shape_fn in [
            lambda t: t,
            lambda t: t.unsqueeze(0),
            lambda t: t.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0),
        ]:
            ro = spectral_rolloff(shape_fn(x))
            assert ro.dim() == 1
            assert (ro >= 0.0).all()
            assert (ro <= 12000.0 + 1.0).all()  # <= Nyquist

        class _FakeModel:
            sample_rate = 24000

            def generate_sound_bank(self, n, steps, seed):
                return [torch.randn(1, 24000) for _ in range(n)]

            def synthesize_midi(self, events, bank, seed=None, **kw):
                t = (
                    torch.arange(self.sample_rate, dtype=torch.float32)
                    / self.sample_rate
                )
                return torch.sin(2 * torch.pi * (220 + 10 * seed) * t)

            def condition_on_audio(self, audio, n, steps, strength, seed):
                return [torch.randn(1, 24000) for _ in range(n)]

        enc = _StubEncoder()
        events = [(60, 0.0, 0.25), (64, 0.25, 0.25)]
        rows = recursive_variant_drift(
            _FakeModel(), events, rounds=2, encoder=enc, device=torch.device("cpu"),
            steps=2, seed=3407, bank_n=2,
        )
        assert len(rows) == 3  # round 0 + 2 recursive rounds
        for r in rows:
            assert {
                "round",
                "centroid_mean_hz",
                "centroid_std_hz",
                "rolloff_mean_hz",
                "clap_distance_to_round0",
            } <= set(r)
            assert r["centroid_mean_hz"] > 0.0
            assert r["rolloff_mean_hz"] > 0.0
            assert r["clap_distance_to_round0"] >= 0.0
        assert rows[0]["round"] == 0
        assert rows[0]["clap_distance_to_round0"] == 0.0
        assert [r["round"] for r in rows] == [0, 1, 2]

    def test_true_recursion_feeds_output_back(self) -> None:
        calls: dict[str, list[object]] = {"condition": [], "synthesize": 0}

        class _FakeModel:
            sample_rate = 24000

            def generate_sound_bank(self, n, steps, seed):
                return [torch.randn(1, 24000) for _ in range(n)]

            def synthesize_midi(self, events, bank, seed=None, **kw):
                calls["synthesize"] = calls["synthesize"] + 1
                t = (
                    torch.arange(self.sample_rate, dtype=torch.float32)
                    / self.sample_rate
                )
                return torch.sin(2 * torch.pi * 300 * t)

            def condition_on_audio(self, audio, n, steps, strength, seed):
                calls["condition"].append(audio)
                return [torch.randn(1, 24000) for _ in range(n)]

        enc = _StubEncoder()
        events = [(60, 0.0, 0.25)]
        recursive_variant_drift(
            _FakeModel(), events, rounds=3, encoder=enc, device=torch.device("cpu"),
            steps=2, seed=3407, bank_n=2,
        )
        # condition_on_audio called once per recursive round...
        assert len(calls["condition"]) == 3
        # ...and each call receives the previous round's RENDER (finite audio)
        for a in calls["condition"]:
            assert isinstance(a, torch.Tensor)
            assert float(a.abs().sum()) > 0.0
        # synthesize called once per round + once for round 0
        assert calls["synthesize"] == 4

def _train_one_graph_decoder(encoder, prior, loaders, args, device, noise_std, epochs):
    """Train a fresh graph decoder on the given prior; return the decoder."""
    loss_fn = ALDSCLoss(
        prior=prior,
        lambda_rec=1.0,
        lambda_stft=0.0,
        lambda_chart=0.5,
        lambda_smooth=0.1,
    )
    dec = GraphDecoder(
        latent_channels=128,
        out_channels=1,
        feature_dim=128,
        base_channels=args.base_channels,
        prior=prior,
        upsample_strides=(2, 4, 5, 8),
    )
    vae = AudioVAE(encoder=encoder, decoder=dec)
    list(
        log_training(
            train_audio_decoder(
                loaders["train"],
                vae,
                prior,
                loss_fn,
                epochs=epochs,
                lr=args.lr,
                device=device,
                noise_std=noise_std,
            ),
            label=f"Graph decoder (q={prior.q}, noise={noise_std})",
        )
    )
    return dec


def _sweep_q(embeddings, encoder, loaders, args, device):
    """q sweep: rebuild prior per q, retrain graph decoder, test L1 + retention."""
    print(f"\n=== Sweep: q ∈ {args.ablation_q} (decoder retraining) ===")
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    epochs = args.sweep_decoder_epochs or args.decoder_epochs
    for q in args.ablation_q:
        print(f"  q={q}: building prior + training decoder...")
        prior_q = build_arrow_prior(embeddings, q=q, k=args.k).to(device)
        dec = _train_one_graph_decoder(
            encoder, prior_q, loaders, args, device, args.noise_inject, epochs
        )
        torch.save(
            dec.state_dict(), ARTIFACTS_DIR / f"{args.tag}graph_dec_q{q}.pt"
        )
        loss_fn_q = ALDSCLoss(
            prior=prior_q,
            lambda_rec=1.0,
            lambda_stft=0.0,
            lambda_chart=0.5,
            lambda_smooth=0.1,
        )
        from ald_sc.eval import evaluate_reconstruction

        m = evaluate_reconstruction(
            encoder, dec, prior_q, loaders["test"], loss_fn_q, device
        )
        ret = band_energy_retention(encoder, dec, prior_q, loaders["test"], device)
        cosine = ret[0]["cosine"] if ret else float("nan")
        rows.append(
            {
                "q": q,
                "test_L1": m["rec"],
                "retention_cosine": cosine,
                "decoder_epochs": epochs,
            }
        )
        print(f"    test L1={m['rec']:.4f} retention_cosine={cosine:.4f}")
    write_csv(_out("sweep_q.csv", args.tag), rows)
    print(f"  wrote sweep_q.csv ({len(rows)} rows)")


def _sweep_noise(prior, encoder, dit, sched, loaders, args, device, main_graph_dec):
    """NOISE_INJECT sweep: fidelity (test L1) vs diversity (variant distance)."""
    print(f"\n=== Sweep: NOISE_INJECT ∈ {args.ablation_noise} ===")
    from ald_sc.eval import evaluate_reconstruction, variant_diversity

    loss_fn = ALDSCLoss(
        prior=prior,
        lambda_rec=1.0,
        lambda_stft=0.0,
        lambda_chart=0.5,
        lambda_smooth=0.1,
    )
    # Fixed conditioning clip from the test split (workflow novelty probe).
    test_clip = next(iter(loaders["test"]))
    test_clip = (
        test_clip if isinstance(test_clip, torch.Tensor) else test_clip[0]
    )[:1].to(device)
    epochs = args.sweep_decoder_epochs or args.decoder_epochs

    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for noise in args.ablation_noise:
        if abs(noise - args.noise_inject) < 1e-9:
            dec = main_graph_dec  # already trained at this noise level
            reused = True
        else:
            print(f"  noise={noise}: training decoder...")
            dec = _train_one_graph_decoder(
                encoder, prior, loaders, args, device, noise, epochs
            )
            torch.save(
                dec.state_dict(), ARTIFACTS_DIR / f"{args.tag}graph_dec_noise{noise}.pt"
            )
            reused = False
        m = evaluate_reconstruction(
            encoder, dec, prior, loaders["test"], loss_fn, device
        )
        model = LSDModel(
            prior=prior, dit=dit, decoder=dec, encoder=encoder, schedule=sched
        )
        variants = model.condition_on_audio(
            test_clip, n=4, steps=args.steps, seed=args.seed
        )
        div = variant_diversity(
            lambda d: variants, [len(variants)], encoder, device
        )[0]
        rows.append(
            {
                "noise_inject": noise,
                "test_L1": m["rec"],
                "variant_distance": div["mean_distance"],
                "reused_main_decoder": reused,
            }
        )
        print(
            f"    noise={noise}: test L1={m['rec']:.4f} "
            f"variant_distance={div['mean_distance']:.5f}"
        )
    write_csv(_out("sweep_noise.csv", args.tag), rows)
    print(f"  wrote sweep_noise.csv ({len(rows)} rows)")

content.text: The criterion is degenerate for backward sampling: `Σ ν_k ᾱ_k(t)` is *lowest* at the noisy start of sampling, so it either fires at step 0 (small-ν priors, as in the smoke run) or never fires (large priors) — never a meaningful tradeoff. The physically-sensible "heat-death stopping" for the reverse process is: stop when the **remaining dissipation** `Σ ν_k (1 − ᾱ_k(t))` falls below ε (nothing measurable left to resolve). Implementing that:

def heat_death_metric(self, t: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        """Heat-death metric (forward direction): Σ ν_k · ᾱ_k(t).

        This approximates the MMSE-weighted entropy rate from the paper.
        At t=0 the metric is high (modes are active); at t=T it approaches 0
        (all modes at equilibrium).

        Parameters
        ----------
        t : Tensor (scalar)
            External time.

        Returns
        -------
        Tensor (scalar)
            Heat-death metric of the forward process.
        """
        ab_k = self.alpha_bar_k(t)
        return (self.nu * ab_k).sum()

    def remaining_dissipation(self, t: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        """Remaining dissipation of the REVERSE process: Σ ν_k · (1 − ᾱ_k(t)).

        During denoising (t: 1 → 0) each mode resolves on its own entropic
        clock; this measures how much spectral structure is still unresolved.
        It is maximal at t=1 (pure noise) and monotonically decreases to 0 as
        sampling completes. Heat death of the reverse process = nothing
        measurable left to resolve: ``remaining_dissipation(t) < eps``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        t : Tensor (scalar)
            External time in [0, 1].

        Returns
        -------
        Tensor (scalar)
            Remaining dissipation, in units of Σ ν_k.
        """
        ab_k = self.alpha_bar_k(t)
        return (self.nu * (1.0 - ab_k)).sum()

    def is_heat_death(self, t: Tensor) -> bool:
        """Intrinsic stopping criterion (reverse process): heat death when
        the remaining dissipation Σ ν_k (1 − ᾱ_k(t)) < ε.

        Parameters
        ----------
        t : Tensor (scalar)
            External time.

        Returns
        -------
        bool
            True if all modes are near equilibrium (nothing left to resolve).
        """

"""Bisect the 96kHz MPS divergence: scale vs on-the-fly-encoding.

Conditions (identical init/data across devices):
  A. CPU-encoded latents (audio_length=96000, T_lat=300), train on CPU  (control)
  B. CPU-encoded latents, train on MPS                                (scale test)
  C. MPS-encoded latents, train on MPS                                (encode-path test)
  D. MPS-encoded latents, train on CPU                                (encode-path control)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
from pathlib import Path

import torch

from ald_sc.audio_codec import EnCodecEncoder
from ald_sc.data import AudioFolderDataset, build_audio_dataloader
from ald_sc.build_prior import build_arrow_prior
from ald_sc.graph_decoder import GraphDecoder
from ald_sc.losses import ALDSCLoss

DATA_ROOT = "data"
N_FILES, BATCH, EPOCHS, LR, NOISE = 64, 8, 12, 1e-3, 0.1
AUDIO_LEN = 96000


def encode_corpus(enc_device: str):
    ds = AudioFolderDataset(root=DATA_ROOT, audio_length=AUDIO_LEN)
    ds.files = ds.files[:N_FILES]
    loader = build_audio_dataloader(ds, batch_size=BATCH, shuffle=False)
    enc = EnCodecEncoder().to(enc_device)
    batches, wavs = [], []
    for x in loader:
        wav = x[0] if isinstance(x, (list, tuple)) else x
        z, A, c_spec = enc.encode(wav.to(enc_device), prior_stub := _PriorStub())
        batches.append(tuple(t.detach().cpu() for t in (z, A, c_spec)))
        wavs.append(wav.cpu())
    # Build the prior from CPU embeddings of the encoded features.
    embeddings = torch.cat([b[1] for b in batches], dim=0)
    prior = build_arrow_prior(embeddings, q=8, k=4)
    return prior, batches, wavs


class _PriorStub(torch.nn.Module):
    """Placeholder prior for encode(); replaced by the real prior afterwards.

    EnCodecEncoder.encode uses prior.chart_energy_descriptor(a) only, so we
    pre-build a prior on random embeddings of the right F and recompute
    c_spec with the REAL prior once built (done by the caller).
    """

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        from ald_sc.build_prior import build_arrow_prior as bap

        p = bap(torch.randn(64, 128), q=8, k=4)
        self.chart_energy_descriptor = p.chart_energy_descriptor


def respec(batches, prior):
    out = []
    for z, A, _c in batches:
        c = prior.chart_energy_descriptor(A)
        out.append((z, A, c))
    return out


def train(prior, data, wavs, dev, label):
    prior = copy.deepcopy(prior).to(dev)
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    dec = GraphDecoder(
        latent_channels=128, out_channels=1, feature_dim=128,
        base_channels=32, prior=prior,
    ).to(dev)
    lf = ALDSCLoss(prior=prior, lambda_rec=1.0, lambda_stft=0.0,
                   lambda_chart=0.5, lambda_smooth=0.1)
    lf.prior = prior
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(dec.parameters(), lr=LR)
    torch.manual_seed(99)
    D = [(z.to(dev), A.to(dev), c.to(dev), w.to(dev)) for (z, A, c), w in zip(data, wavs)]
    means = []
    dec.train()
    for ep in range(EPOCHS):
        els = []
        for z, A, c_spec, wav in D:
            opt.zero_grad()
            zi = z + NOISE * torch.randn_like(z)
            xh = dec(zi, c_spec)
            loss = lf(wav, xh, A, A.detach())["total"]
            loss.backward()
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(dec.parameters(), 1.0)
            opt.step()
            els.append(loss.item())
        means.append(sum(els) / len(els))
    print(f"[{label:>28}] " + " ".join(f"{v:.2f}" for v in means))
    return means


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Encoding on CPU...")
    prior_c, batches_c, wavs = encode_corpus("cpu")
    print("Encoding on MPS...")
    prior_m, batches_m, _ = encode_corpus("mps")
    dz = (batches_c[0][0] - batches_m[0][0]).abs()
    print(f"latent diff CPU-vs-MPS encode: mean={dz.mean():.3e} max={dz.max():.3e} "
          f"(z std={batches_c[0][0].std():.3f})")
    print(f"prior eigvals cpu: {[f'{v:.3f}' for v in prior_c.eigvals_q.tolist()]}")
    print(f"prior eigvals mps: {[f'{v:.3f}' for v in prior_m.eigvals_q.tolist()]}")

    data_c = respec(batches_c, prior_c)
    data_m = respec(batches_m, prior_m)
    train(prior_c, data_c, wavs, "cpu", "A: cpu-encode, train CPU")
    train(prior_c, data_c, wavs, "mps", "B: cpu-encode, train MPS")
    train(prior_m, data_m, wavs, "mps", "C: mps-encode, train MPS")
    train(prior_m, data_m, wavs, "cpu", "D: mps-encode, train CPU")

"""Per-step probe: replicate the runner's graph-decoder training on MPS,
log every step's loss + grad norm, and find the first explosive step.

Then: for the trigger batch, compare CPU vs MPS forward/backward with
IDENTICAL weights and inputs to isolate the diverging op.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import random

import torch

from ald_sc.audio_codec import EnCodecEncoder
from ald_sc.build_prior import build_arrow_prior
from ald_sc.data import AudioFolderDataset, build_audio_dataloader
from ald_sc.graph_decoder import GraphDecoder
from ald_sc.losses import ALDSCLoss
from ald_sc.eval import split_files

DATA_ROOT = "data"
SEED = 3407


def main():
    random.seed(SEED)
    torch.manual_seed(SEED)
    device = torch.device("mps")

    all_files = sorted(__import__("pathlib").Path(DATA_ROOT).glob("*.wav"))
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    selected = rng.sample(all_files, 256)
    train_files, val_files, test_files = split_files(selected, 0.7, 0.15, seed=SEED)

    ds = AudioFolderDataset(root=DATA_ROOT, audio_length=96000)
    ds.files = train_files
    loader = build_audio_dataloader(ds, batch_size=8, shuffle=True)

    encoder = EnCodecEncoder()
    prior_ds = AudioFolderDataset(root=DATA_ROOT, audio_length=96000)
    prior_ds.files = train_files
    prior_loader = build_audio_dataloader(prior_ds, batch_size=8, shuffle=False)
    feats = [encoder.extract_features(b).mean(dim=2) for b in prior_loader]
    embeddings = torch.cat(feats, dim=0).cpu()
    prior = build_arrow_prior(embeddings, q=8, k=4).to(device)

    torch.manual_seed(SEED)
    dec = GraphDecoder(
        latent_channels=128, out_channels=1, feature_dim=128,
        base_channels=32, prior=prior, upsample_strides=(2, 4, 5, 8),
    ).to(device)
    loss_fn = ALDSCLoss(prior=prior, lambda_rec=1.0, lambda_stft=0.0,
                        lambda_chart=0.5, lambda_smooth=0.1)
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(dec.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    dec.train()
    encoder = encoder.to(device)

    print("step  loss      grad_norm  batch_max_z")
    trigger = None
    step = 0
    for ep in range(2):
        for batch in loader:
            x = batch if isinstance(batch, torch.Tensor) else batch[0]
            x = x.to(device)
            opt.zero_grad()
            z, A, c_spec = encoder.encode(x, prior)
            z = z + 0.1 * torch.randn_like(z)
            xh = dec(z, c_spec)
            loss = loss_fn(x, xh, A, A.detach())["total"]
            loss.backward()
            gn = float(torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(dec.parameters(), 1.0))
            opt.step()
            lv = float(loss.item())
            if step < 6 or lv > 1.0 or (step % 10 == 0):
                print(f"{step:4d}  {lv:.4f}  {gn:9.3f}  {float(z.abs().max()):8.2f}")
            if lv > 1.0 and trigger is None:
                trigger = (step, ep, copy.deepcopy(x.cpu()))
            step += 1
        if trigger is not None:

        print("no explosion within probe horizon")
        return

    step, ep, x_bad = trigger
    print(f"\ntrigger step = {step} (epoch {ep})")

    # Replay: identical weights + the trigger batch, CPU vs MPS.
    torch.manual_seed(1)
    dec_c = GraphDecoder(
        latent_channels=128, out_channels=1, feature_dim=128,
        base_channels=32, prior=prior.cpu(), upsample_strides=(2, 4, 5, 8),
    )
    enc_cpu = EnCodecEncoder()

    torch.manual_seed(2)  # same noise
    for dev, d, e in (("cpu", dec_c, enc_cpu),):
        z, A, c_spec = e.encode(x_bad, prior.cpu())
        torch.manual_seed(2)
        noise = 0.1 * torch.randn_like(z)
        xh = d(z + noise, c_spec)
        loss = ALDSCLoss(prior=prior.cpu(), lambda_rec=1.0, lambda_stft=0.0,
                         lambda_chart=0.5, lambda_smooth=0.1)(x_bad, xh, A, A.detach())
        loss["total"].backward()
        print(f"{dev}: loss={float(loss['total']):.4f} "
              f"rec={float(loss['rec']):.4f} "
              f"gn={float(torch.sqrt(sum(p.grad.pow(2).sum() for p in d.parameters()))):.3f}")

    torch.manual_seed(2)

    xh_m = dec_m(z_m + noise_m, c_m)
    loss_m = ALDSCLoss(prior=prior.to("mps"), lambda_rec=1.0, lambda_stft=0.0,
                       lambda_chart=0.5, lambda_smooth=0.1)(
        x_bad.to("mps"), xh_m, A_m, A_m.detach())
    loss_m["total"].backward()
    print(f"mps: loss={float(loss_m['total']):.4f} rec={float(loss_m['rec']):.4f} "
          f"gn={float(torch.sqrt(sum(p.grad.pow(2).sum() for p in dec_m.parameters()))):.3f}")

content.text:
**Found it**: with wave-block gradients frozen, MPS is perfectly stable under full noise. The pathology is the **time-constant delta broadcast**: a per-channel constant entering GroupNorm is shift-invariant in forward, so its *gradient* is carried entirely by second-order 1/σ terms — enormous when a group's temporal variance is small. That's why neither clipping, eps, warmup, nor small-init helped: it's the gradient *direction*, not magnitude.

The structural fix is also the more faithful design: apply the chart round-trip **per time-step** (a true graph-filter step over activations, as the module docs describe) via 1×1 convs instead of pooled Linear + broadcast:

def forward(self, h: Tensor, c_spec: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        """Apply wave-based reconstruction.

        Parameters
        ----------
        h : Tensor (B, C, T)
            Feature activations (1-D temporal).
        c_spec : Tensor (B, 3*q)
            Spectral conditioning vector [ẽ, λ_chart, ν].

        Returns
        -------
        Tensor (B, C, T)
        """
        # Per-time-step projection to feature space: (B, C, T) -> (B, F, T)
        a = self.feature_to_chart(h)

        # Project to chart: (B, F, T) @ (F, q) -> (B, q, T)
        h_hat = torch.einsum("bft,fq->bqt", a, self.U_q)

        # Gate by dispersion: (B, 3q) -> (B, q)
        g = torch.sigmoid(self.gate(c_spec))

        # Gated projection (gate is clip-level, broadcast over time)
        gated = h_hat * g.unsqueeze(-1)

        # Lift back to feature space: (B, q, T) @ (q, F) -> (B, F, T)
        a_recon = torch.einsum("bqt,qf->bft", gated, self.U_q.T)

        # Map back to channel space: (B, F, T) -> (B, C, T)
        delta = self.chart_to_feature(a_recon)

        h_modulated = h + delta

        h_out = h + self.conv(self.act(self.norm(h_modulated)))

        return h_out
input.oldString:
def forward(self, h: Tensor, c_spec: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        """Apply wave-based reconstruction.

        Parameters
        ----------
        h : Tensor (B, C, T)
            Feature activations (1-D temporal).
        c_spec : Tensor (B, 3*q)
            Spectral conditioning vector [ẽ, λ_chart, ν].

        Returns
        -------
        Tensor (B, C, T)
        """
        # Pool over temporal axis: (B, C, T) -> (B, C)
        pooled = h.mean(dim=2)

        # Project to feature space: (B, C) -> (B, F)
        a = self.feature_to_chart(pooled)

        # Project to chart: (B, F) @ (F, q) -> (B, q)
        h_hat = a @ self.U_q

        # Gate by dispersion: (B, 3q) -> (B, q)
        g = torch.sigmoid(self.gate(c_spec))

        # Gated projection
        gated = h_hat * g

        # Lift back to feature space: (B, q) @ (q, F) -> (B, F)
        a_recon = gated @ self.U_q.T

        # Map back to channel space: (B, F) -> (B, C)
        delta = self.chart_to_feature(a_recon)

        # Broadcast over temporal axis: (B, C) -> (B, C, 1)
        delta = delta.unsqueeze(-1)

        h_modulated = h + delta

        h_out = h + self.conv(self.act(self.norm(h_modulated)))

        return h_out

def test_heat_death_criterion(self) -> None:
        """Reverse-process heat death: Σ ν_k · (1 − ᾱ_k(t)) < ε.

        During denoising (t: 1 → 0) remaining dissipation decreases from
        Σ ν_k (pure noise, nothing resolved) to 0 (sampling complete), so
        heat death fires at t=0 and never at t=1. The previous forward-time
        criterion Σ ν_k ᾱ_k(t) < ε fired at the START of sampling (t≈1),
        which made the stopping criterion degenerate in the samplers.
        """
        prior = _make_prior(f=32, q=8)
        sched = SpectralSchedule(prior, horizon=1.0, eps=1e-3)
        # At t=0 sampling is complete: nothing left to resolve
        assert sched.is_heat_death(torch.tensor(0.0))
        # At t=1 (pure noise) all modes are unresolved: not heat death
        assert not sched.is_heat_death(torch.tensor(1.0))

    def test_remaining_dissipation_monotone(self) -> None:
        """Remaining dissipation decreases as the reverse process proceeds."""
        prior = _make_prior(f=32, q=8)
        sched = SpectralSchedule(prior, horizon=1.0)
        ts = torch.linspace(0.99, 0.01, 20)
        vals = [sched.remaining_dissipation(t).item() for t in ts]
        for i in range(1, len(vals)):
            assert vals[i] <= vals[i - 1] + 1e-6, (
                "Remaining dissipation should be non-increasing as t -> 0"
            )

content.text: Notable: with the per-time-step graph filter, the graph decoder now *slightly beats* the baseline on L1 across all splits (test 0.1127 vs 0.1151). While sweeps run, correcting the record on issue #51 — my earlier conclusion was wrong:

input.command:
cat > /var/folders/jp/_9hztzgd13s81lhsr83dn6y00000gn/T/opencode/mps-correction.md <<'EOF'
## Correction: the divergence is real, reproducible, and now root-caused — my earlier "doesn't reproduce" conclusion was wrong

Re-running the full eval pipeline on MPS (issue #50) reproduced the divergence at the runner's config (96 kHz audio / T_lat=300 / `base_channels=32`): loss 0.83 → 17.8 over 20 epochs while CPU stayed at 0.199 → 0.172 — **with grad clipping already active**. My earlier bisection missed it because the repro used different hparams (24 kHz, `base_channels=64`, precomputed latents) whose loss landscape avoided the pathology. The "collateral of the EnCodec device bug" conclusion above is retracted.

### What it actually is (bisected stepwise, identical seeds/init/data)

1. **Per-op device parity holds** (unchanged from above: ≤1e-6 fwd/bwd everywhere; identical replay of any single batch matches across devices).
2. With latent noise injection **disabled**, CPU and MPS trajectories are **identical to 4 decimals** and both stable.
3. With noise on, the trajectory diverges after **one Adam step**: same step-0 loss/grad (0.4397 / 14.5) on both devices; step-1 grad norm 4.5 (CPU) vs 447 (MPS). A 0.0045-std noise (0.1% of latent scale) at step 1 flips the gradient from 4.3 → 4301 at *identical weights*. CPU and MPS generate **different RNG streams** (`randn` differs per backend), so which trajectory falls in is chance — the landscape itself has a knife-edge.
4. Freezing `wave_blocks` parameters → MPS fully stable under full noise.
5. Grad clip@1, GroupNorm `eps` up to 1e-2, noise warmup, and 0.01× small-init of the delta projection all **fail** to fix it.

### Root cause

The old `WaveReconstructionBlock` projected the **temporal-mean** of `h` through the `U_q` chart round-trip and broadcast the result as a **time-constant per-channel delta**: `h + delta` entering `GroupNorm(8)`. GroupNorm is shift-invariant in the forward pass (a group-mean shift is removed), so the *gradient* w.r.t. that constant is carried entirely by second-order terms ∝ 1/σ³ — enormous whenever a channel group has small temporal variance (common with smooth EnCodec latents). That makes early training a coin-flip between a stable basin and an exploding-gradient basin, decided by the device's noise stream. It was never an MPS numerics bug — CPU seeds can hit it too (the same fragility class explains the earlier "n0.0 uptick" observation).

### Fix (per-time-step graph filter)

`WaveReconstructionBlock` now applies the chart round-trip at **every time step** via 1×1 convs + einsum against `U_q` — no temporal pooling, no time-constant broadcast. This is also more faithful to the documented design ("project feature activations onto the chart basis"; a graph-filter step over the activation field). The delta projection keeps a 0.01× near-identity init.

Validated on the exact failing config (MPS, full noise, 96 kHz):
- probe: grads 14 → 1–3, loss 0.45 → 0.14 (was 0.44 → 17.8)
- full runner: graph decoder trains cleanly on MPS, and at 20 epochs the graph decoder now **slightly beats** the baseline on L1 (test 0.1127 vs 0.1151) where the pooled version lost (0.117 vs 0.114)

All 223 tests green; `tests/test_device_parity.py` still passes. Paper numbers are being re-run on MPS in the issue #50 loop. The "MPS parity" tests remain valid — the divergence was trajectory-level, not op-level, which is exactly why op parity alone didn't catch it.
EOF

"""Re-run the heat-death eps sweep with properly scaled absolute thresholds.

The prior's remaining-dissipation scale is Sum(nu_k) ~= 5.4, and the 50-step
DDIM grid checks t in {0.98, ..., 0.02}; eps below ~0.1 can never fire before
the budget ends. This sweep uses eps in {0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0} (absolute,
documented against Sum(nu)) via the saved artifacts in results/artifacts/.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
from pathlib import Path

import torch

from ald_sc.audio_codec import BaselineAudioDecoder, EnCodecEncoder
from ald_sc.build_prior import build_arrow_prior
from ald_sc.data import AudioFolderDataset, build_audio_dataloader
from ald_sc.dit import MinimalDiT
from ald_sc.eval import encodec_pooled_features, eps_sweep, split_files, write_csv
from ald_sc.graph_decoder import GraphDecoder
from ald_sc.schedule import CosineSchedule

SEED = 3407
ART = Path("results/artifacts")

random.seed(SEED)
torch.manual_seed(SEED)
device = torch.device("mps")

all_files = sorted(Path("data").glob("*.wav"))
selected = random.Random(SEED).sample(all_files, 256)
_, _, test_files = split_files(selected, 0.7, 0.15, seed=SEED)
test_ds = AudioFolderDataset(root="data", audio_length=96000)
test_ds.files = test_files
test_loader = build_audio_dataloader(test_ds, batch_size=8, shuffle=False)

encoder = EnCodecEncoder()
embeddings = torch.load(ART / "embeddings.pt", weights_only=False)
prior = build_arrow_prior(embeddings, q=8, k=4).to(device)
print(f"Sum(nu_k) = {prior.eigvals_q.sum().item():.3f}")

graph_dec = GraphDecoder(
    latent_channels=128, out_channels=1, feature_dim=128, base_channels=32,
    prior=prior, upsample_strides=(2, 4, 5, 8),
)
graph_dec.load_state_dict(torch.load(ART / "graph_dec.pt", weights_only=False))
dit = MinimalDiT(
    latent_channels=128, latent_length=96000 // 320, patch_size=8, dim=64,
    depth=2, num_heads=4, spec_dim=3 * 8,
)
dit.load_state_dict(torch.load(ART / "dit.pt", weights_only=False))
sched = CosineSchedule(num_steps=1000)

ref_feats = encodec_pooled_features(
    (b for b in test_loader), encoder, device
)

rows = eps_sweep(
    dit, sched, prior, graph_dec, encoder, ref_feats,
    [0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0], device,
    n_gen=16, steps=50, seed=SEED,
)
for r in rows:
    print(f"  eps={r['eps']:5.2f}: steps={r['mean_steps']:5.1f} FAD={r['FAD']:.2f}")
write_csv(Path("results/sweep_eps.csv"), rows)
print("wrote results/sweep_eps.csv")

# Autoresearch Summary — Issue #50 Phase 1: eval extensions + MPS rerun

`[autoresearch] mode: orchestrator (build-feature) → CONVERGED`

## Calibration (user direction)
The paper presents a **novel paradigm** (dehydration → diffusion → rehydration →
recursive variation) at preliminary scale. All tables are hypothesis-generating
evidence with honest numbers and documented proxy methodology — no benchmark
claims. Workflow-affordance metrics (compression, coherence, variant drift,
diversity-vs-fidelity, intrinsic stopping) stand alongside fidelity metrics.

## What was built / changed
- **`src/ald_sc/eval.py`** extensions: `band_energy_retention` (§6.2 per-band
  retention), `spectral_rolloff` (§6.1 rolloff drift), `recursive_variant_drift`
  (TRUE R-round recursion via `condition_on_audio` → `synthesize_midi`,
  replacing the MIDI-rotation hack), `eps_sweep` (heat-death ε, sampling-only).
  +11 unit tests (`tests/test_eval.py`, 41 total).
- **`scripts/run_evaluation.py`**: `--ablation-q/-noise/-eps` sweep modes,
  `--tag` dataset prefix (ESC-50 tables don't clobber NSynth), checkpoints to
  `results/artifacts/` (gitignored), retention + true recursion integrated,
  eps sweep writes FAD-vs-steps.
- **Heat-death criterion fixed** (`SpectralSchedule.is_heat_death`): the old
  forward-time metric Σνᵏᾱ(t) < ε fired at the *start* of sampling; now the
  reverse-process remaining dissipation Σνᵏ(1−ᾱ(t)) < ε (monotone decreasing
  during denoising). `docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md` + tests updated.
- **Graph decoder v2 (issue #51 root cause found during this loop)**: the wave
  block's pooled/time-constant `U_q` delta broadcast through GroupNorm carried
  1/σ³ gradients (knife-edge; device RNG stream decided stability). Now a
  **per-time-step graph filter** (1×1 convs + einsum through `U_q`, 0.01×
  near-identity init). Correction posted on issue #51; README updated.

## Runs (all `--device mps`, grad-clip 1.0, 256-subset, 20 epochs, real EnCodec)
- Main NSynth run ~15 min (was ~16.5 min CPU) incl. sweeps; ESC-50 run ~20 min.
- ESC-50 downloaded to `data/esc50/` (gitignored; 2000 clips, CC BY 4.0).

## Key results (NSynth)
| Metric | Graph | Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| L1 train / val / test | **0.1103 / 0.1073 / 0.1127** | 0.1162 / 0.1086 / 0.1151 |
| Band-retention cosine (test) | **0.9979** | 0.9969 |
| FAD-proxy (lower better) | 1197.8 | **407.9** |
| CLAP-proxy | **-0.046** | -0.073 |

The per-time-step graph filter **flips the L1 comparison**: graph now ≤
baseline on every split (the pooled version lost 0.117 vs 0.114). Honest
negative retained: FAD-proxy still favours the baseline at this scale.

- λ_ED ablation delta: train 8.6e-4, val −8.8e-5, test −2.7e-5 (still a no-op —
  consistent with the postmortem).
- True recursion (R=4): CLAP-proxy distance to round 0 = 0 → 0.079 → 0.084 →
  0.095 → 0.081 (drift-then-saturate); centroid 606 → 1536 Hz, rolloff 12 →
  584 Hz. Real drift where the old MIDI-rotation metric read ~0.
- q sweep (decoder retrained per q): test L1 0.1087–0.1144 across q ∈
  {4,8,16,32} — flat; reconstruction is not chart-limited at this scale.
- NOISE_INJECT sweep: test L1 0.1116 → 0.1212 (0 → 0.5); variant distance
  6.8e-5 → 2.4e-4 — a weak, non-monotone dial at this scale (honest finding).
- ε sweep (absolute units; Σνᵏ = 5.67): 46 steps/FAD 1154 (ε=0.1) → 41/858
  (ε=0.5) → 37/883 → 30/955 → 12/1180 (ε=5). Intrinsic stopping cuts compute
  2–4× and *improves* the FAD-proxy mid-range. Note: the issue's proposed
  1e-2…1e-4 is below the 50-step grid's reachable resolution — documented.

## Key results (ESC-50, `esc50_`-tagged tables)
- Graph L1 ≤ baseline again (train 0.0818 vs 0.0833; val 0.0794).

54: \begin{abstract}
55: We introduce \emph{Spectral Composition}, a novel method for sample-based
56: music production that treats composition as iterative navigation of a
57: compressed spectral latent manifold rather than direct waveform or
58: symbolic editing. A frozen ArrowSpace graph Laplacian $L_F$ and its
59: associated energy-dispersion network $\lambda^{\mathrm{ED}}$, estimated
60: once from the producer's entire sample library, define a low-dimensional
61: feature-space manifold over which all generative and compositional
62: operations are performed. The method proceeds in four stages:
63: \textbf{(1)~spectral encoding} (``dehydration'') of the library into a
64: compact spectral representation $(L_F, U_q, \lambda^{\mathrm{ED}})$;
65: \textbf{(2)~dense unconditional sampling} of a sound bank via a
66: spectrally-conditioned 1-D diffusion transformer (DiT) operating on
67: EnCodec audio latents; \textbf{(3)~MIDI-conditioned materialisation}
68: (``rehydration'') that pitch-shifts and re-timbres generated sounds
69: according to a language-model-generated MIDI file; and \textbf{(4)~recursive
70: variant generation} by feeding outputs back through the model with
71: successive MIDI sequences. The resulting family of variants, each sharing
72: spectral lineage with the source library, forms a natural set of stems
73: for multitrack mixing. Spectral Composition is built on the
74: Latent Sound Diffusion (LSD) system~\cite{lsd}, which is a
75: sound-production fork of ArrowSpace Latent Diffusion with Spectral Chart
76: Conditioning (ALD-SC)~\cite{aldsc}, and is exposed to the producer via
77: the LSD-Studio desktop application~\cite{lsdstudio}.
78: \end{abstract}

84: %% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
85: \section{Introduction}
86: \label{sec:intro}
87: %% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
88: 
89: Traditional sample-based music production treats a sample library as a
90: fixed, enumerable set of audio assets: the producer browses, triggers,
91: slices, and layers clips inside a digital audio workstation (DAW), guided
92: by perception and taste. This workflow has scaled to industrial size
93: through large commercial sample libraries, but it fundamentally limits
94: compositional novelty to recombination of existing clips without access
95: to the generative structure of the collection.
96: 
97: Spectral Composition proposes a different model: the sample library is a
98: \emph{corpus} from which a frozen spectral prior is estimated once, after
99: which composition is an act of sampling and recombination inside the
100: resulting latent manifold. This reframes ``browsing samples'' as
101: ``traversing a spectral graph'', and ``arranging a track'' as
102: ``recursively rehydrating dense latent draws against symbolic control
103: signals.''
104: 
105: \subsection{Contributions}
106: 
107: \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
108:   \item We define the Spectral Composition pipeline: a four-stage method
109:     (dehydration, sampling, materialisation, recursion) that operationalises
110:     compositional workflows over a spectral latent manifold.
111:   \item We show how the existing LSD inference contract
112:     (\texttt{generate\_sound\_bank}, \texttt{condition\_on\_audio},
113:     \texttt{synthesize\_midi}) directly implements stages~2--4 of the
114:     pipeline, requiring only the addition of a language-model MIDI
115:     front-end.
116:   \item We articulate the mathematical and architectural foundations of the
117:     method, grounding them in the ALD-SC research programme's central
118:     claim: decoding on the feature-space manifold $(L_F,
119:     \lambda^{\mathrm{ED}})$ yields better global semantic coherence under
120:     compression than decoding on an unconstrained ambient latent.
121:   \item We describe LSD-Studio as the producer-facing realisation of the
122:     pipeline, assigning multitrack mixing and workflow management to the
123:     application layer.
124: \end{itemize}
125: 
126: \subsection{Paper Organisation}
127: 
128: Section~\ref{sec:background} reviews background in latent diffusion for
129: audio, ArrowSpace graph priors, and entropic time scheduling.
130: Section~\ref{sec:method} defines the four stages of Spectral Composition.
131: Section~\ref{sec:architecture} describes the underlying model architecture.
132: Section~\ref{sec:implementation} details the implementation and datasets.
133: Section~\ref{sec:evaluation} presents evaluation methodology.
134: Section~\ref{sec:discussion} discusses the method as a creative paradigm.
135: Section~\ref{sec:futurework} outlines future work, and
136: Section~\ref{sec:conclusion} concludes.
